entries.label: T-shirt
entries.definition: Owner-confirmed T-shirt product identity, with short or long sleeves. The canonical parent supplies sleeve-category structure; the subtype does not imply a particular neckline, fabric, fit or colour.
entries.qualification_limit: A generic top, knitted fabric, crew/V neck, filename or a T-shirt name alone is insufficient. Do not infer short sleeves from the subtype.

entries.label: Polo shirt
entries.definition: Owner-confirmed polo-shirt product identity, with a collar and short partial front placket. Short and long sleeve parents are both supported.
entries.qualification_limit: A collar alone or a drawing with an ambiguous front line is insufficient. Full-front shirt opening is not this declared identity. Bare polo only matches in a garment-request noun position; play polo does not.

entries.label: Button-up shirt
entries.definition: Owner-confirmed shirt product identity with a full front button opening, rather than a blouse or polo product identity. No neckline, tailoring or material requirement is inferred.
entries.qualification_limit: Button front or collar alone does not distinguish a blouse. Button-down is not an alias: it can describe a collar distinction that this registry does not verify.

entries.label: Knit / sweater top
entries.definition: Owner-confirmed sweater-style knit-top product identity, excluding T-shirt, polo, button-up shirt and blouse identities. Construction details remain separate qualified description fields.
entries.qualification_limit: Not every knitted textile is a knit_top. Wool, warmth, ribbing or a name alone does not establish this product identity.

entries.label: Blouse
entries.definition: Explicit owner-confirmed blouse product identity. It may have a collar, buttons, different sleeve lengths or many fabrics. Its project eligibility treatment is the separately approved wearer policy.
entries.qualification_limit: Colour, floral pattern, silk, image appearance, name, filename or broad top category cannot establish blouse. If the owner cannot distinguish the product identity, retain Unspecified rather than infer.

unknown: Unknown/Unspecified is an evidence state with null value, never a positive subtype identifier or an allowed-type fallback.
disambiguation: These five mutually exclusive project product identities require an explicit owner declaration. They are not an exhaustive universal garment taxonomy or a claim of independently verified visual truth. If multiple identities appear plausible, record Unspecified; do not resolve using gender, material, pattern or a ranking result.
source_requirement: Authenticated owner review of the actual current garment/processing item, with current category/media, captured registry digest, event/revision and source provenance. Existing B0 qualification/currentness principles apply through a separate immutable channel.
automatic_sources: No supported subtype model mapping currently exists. No model output is promoted. Future emitter/mapping/quality approval is a separate contract; unsupported suggestions stay non-qualifying.
other_parents: The other eleven canonical categories have no subtype obligation in registry v1, unless unresolved earlier blouse evidence requires a separately audited correction.
legacy_bare_shirt: Exact existing broad upper-category meaning is retained; it does not establish any of these five subtypes.
excluded_distinctions: marketing dark shades without existing precise colour evidence
